name: LiteTV Channels
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.

versions.changelog: Fixes a channel built from series showing nothing but "Sendepause": episodes filed under season 0 were dropped, and a library where that is where the episodes sit left the channel with nothing to play. Specials now air where their metadata says they belong - between the episodes they were made for - instead of being skipped. Scheduling grew up: program blocks give a part of the week its own lineup and its own weekdays, programs can start on a fixed grid so a block can promise the film at 20:15, a queue can be shuffled once and for good, and the time a slot leaves over is filled with trailers for what is coming up. The guide is now a real time grid, and the channels can be published to Jellyfin's own Live TV section so native clients get a schedule too.

Fixes published channels flashing between the player and the menu without ever playing, which the previous release caused: the follow-up program was handed to the client as a queued item, but a client that starts it immediately instead of queuing it turns that into an endless loop. Channels no longer do this. A channel is also a single entry again rather than a folder of separate films to start - it switches on and joins what is on air, and the schedule is written in its description where it can be read in order and not played by accident.

Channel listings show every program with the time it airs, instead of marking one of them as running now. The marker could not stay true: an entry's label is written once and never rewritten, so it stayed on a program that had long finished.

Programs on a published channel now follow each other smoothly. The next program is put into the client's own queue as soon as one starts playing, so the channel rolls on from there instead of dropping back to the menu for a moment while the server sends the next one. Should a client ignore the queue, the server still steps in as before.

A published channel now lists its schedule instead of just the one program on air: opening a channel shows what is running and what follows, in order, with start times. Every entry is playable - the one on air joins live, a later one starts from its beginning.

Fixes published channels stopping at the end of a program on TV apps: looking up the follow-up entry asked the channel manager for a folder without naming its channel, which threw. Channel entries also carry their media details now - container, streams, the lot - instead of only resolving them when playback starts, since a player that is told nothing about the media may refuse to start it.

Published channels keep running on their own: when a program ends, the next one is handed to the client, so a channel started from a TV app carries on like the web UI does. Channels also no longer collect a resume position of their own, which was putting every channel into Continue Watching and leaving it there. Fixes published channels playing the program that was on when they were first opened: the server resolves an item's media only once, so each program now gets its own entry.

Channels are now published to Jellyfin itself, so they can be browsed and played on every client instead of only in the web UI: a "TV-Sender" entry appears in the library, with one folder per channel holding whatever is on air. Playing it joins the channel at the live position - the program's own file plays directly, nothing is streamed or transcoded by the plugin. Can be switched off in the plugin settings.

Media watched outside a channel now keeps its watch state even when that same title happens to be on air: a channel only covers the device it is playing on, so starting the title deliberately somewhere else records normally. Leaving a channel also stops holding back watch state for half a minute - the program is released three seconds after its playback actually stops, so watching it properly straight afterwards is recorded right away. A client that disappears without reporting a stop no longer keeps its program covered either, since the session ending releases it.

Fixes registration with the File Transformation plugin, which had been failing on every startup: the plugin shipped its own copy of Newtonsoft.Json, so the payload it built was a different type than the one File Transformation expected, despite the identical name. The payload is now built through that plugin's own type and the duplicate library is no longer shipped at all. Script injection previously fell back to request-time middleware, which kept working, so this only restores the preferred path.

Fixes channel viewing still showing up as watched even though nothing was written to the database: the server hands out one cached watch-state object per item, and everything that records playback changes that object before asking for it to be saved - so blocking the save alone left the item marked played in memory until the next server restart. While a program airs on a channel the plugin now hands out a copy, so those changes land nowhere at all.

Watch state is no longer recorded and cleaned up afterwards - while a program airs on a channel, its played flag, play count, resume position and last-played date are simply never written. This works below the player, so it covers every client and every way playback was started, and nothing flickers through Continue Watching or Next Up in the meantime. Programs now also play out in full instead of being cut short before the credits, the 'Als Nächstes' countdown follows the player (it holds while paused and moves along when you seek) and the hand-off waits while paused, and there is a 'next program' button on the pause panel and on the end-of-item overlay.

Fixes watch state still leaking from the second program onwards: the stop of the item that just ended dropped the protection for the follow-up the channel had already prepared, so everything after the first program was marked watched and piled up in Continue Watching. Replaying a program ('Von Anfang an') and channels cast to another device (which never snapshotted at all) are protected too, closing the tab now leaves the channel cleanly instead of stranding the current program as watched, and a program the viewer starts themselves is no longer touched.

Channels can interleave their sources in blocks: set 'Episodes per block' (e.g. 2) so two series air alternating, S1E1, S1E2, S2E1, S2E2, ... (0 keeps the marathon behaviour). Watch state is now fully protected: each item's played flag, play count and resume position are snapshotted before playback and restored on stop and on leaving, so channel viewing never marks anything watched. Returning to the home page now also leaves the channel cleanly.

Channels no longer stop after one item: the schedule now follows continuously from item to item (Jellyfin swaps media in place without a view change, which the previous watcher missed). The TV home-screen row is placed in the normal sections flow, removing the large gap above it. Fixes a tuned-state leak when leaving the channel after an in-place advance.

The header 📺 button now has its own setting, independent of the home row and overlays, so it can be hidden while the TV row and playback overlays stay on. 'Enable the TV UI' remains the master switch.

Skipping ahead no longer stops the channel: the schedule keeps following item to item even when episodes are finished early. The follow-up now also starts precisely at the credits using Jellyfin's Media Segments (outro) when available, falling back to a short margin before the end otherwise, so the tail credits are skipped.

The TV home-screen row no longer flickers when returning to the home page: the channel guide is cached and the row is only rebuilt when the schedule actually changes. The end-of-episode overlay also hides its choice buttons when following the schedule and continuing the series lead to the same next episode.

TV row stays at the bottom of the home screen; pause panel synced with Jellyfin Enhanced's pause screen and positioned top-right; end-of-episode overlay hides its buttons when there is no series to continue.

Overlay buttons no longer toggle play/pause; Next Up suppressed while tuned; watch state fully untouched; skipping ahead advances the schedule; earlier end-of-episode overlay; pause panel (Jellyfin Enhanced integration); channel suggestions in the settings; polished visuals; plugin icon.
Initial release: continuous-loop channels, live tune-in in the web client, end-of-episode continue/schedule overlay, watch-state hygiene, play-on-device for native clients.
